title: Gene Expression Analysis of Endothelial Cells Exposed to Shear Stress Using Multiple Parallel-plate Flow Chambers
protocol: Choose an exogenous reference RNA that does not exist in the species or model of interest.
Prepare exogenous reference RNA at least 48 hours prior to RNA extraction.
Obtain or manufacture a cDNA clone of the chosen exogenous reference RNA, such as a firefly luciferase cDNA clone in a plasmid vector.
Perform restriction enzyme digestion of 1 µg of full-length plasmid using XhoI in 1.5-mL microfuge tubes.
Choose an RE that is a single cutter at the 3' end of the exogenous reference RNA sequence, leaving a 5' overhang or blunt end.
Measure the plasmid concentration using spectrophotometry or spectrofluorometry.
Prepare an RE mixture in each tube: add 4 µL of XhoI (20,000 units/mL), 8 µL of RE buffer, x µL of plasmid (1 µg), and sufficient H2O to reach a total solution of 80 µL.
Incubate the RE mixture for 2 h at 37 °C.
Heat inactivate the reaction mixture for 20 min at 65 °C.
Add 4 µL of 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0 to the RE mix.
Add 8 µL of 3 M sodium acetate pH 5.2 to the RE mix.
Add 184 µL of 100% ethanol to the RE mix.
Mix well and freeze the mixture at -20 °C for 30 min.
Spin down the mixture at 4 °C for 20 min at a relative centrifugal force (RCF) of 16,100 x g.
Remove the supernatant with a fine tip without touching the pellet.
Air-dry the pellet for 5 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 6 µL of H2O warmed to 37 °C by pipetting up and down 5x - 10x.

Confirm the linearization of luciferase plasmid by running the digested product on a 2% agarose gel containing ethidium bromide (EtBr) along with a 1 kb+ ladder, a supercoiled ladder, and cut and uncut plasmid.
Perform in vitro transcription using an in vitro transcription method as per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Combine all in vitro transcribed products into a single 1.5-mL polypropylene tube prior to purification.
Purify in vitro transcribed products with an in vitro transcription clean-up kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Assess RNA concentration by measuring absorbance at 260 nm using spectrophotometry.
Dilute stock RNA to a concentration of 1 µg/µL if it is > 1 µg/µL.
Aliquot 1 µL of RNA into PCR tubes for experimental use.
Store the aliquoted RNA samples at -80 °C.
Preheat the oven to 250 °C.
Wrap each glass slide twice with aluminum foil using sterile gloves, avoiding direct contact with the surface of the slide.
Bake the slides in the oven for 1 hour at 250 °C and allow them to cool to room temperature.
Make a fibronectin stock solution of 1 mg/mL with distilled water and incubate it for 30 minutes at 37 °C to dissolve.
Prepare 100-μL aliquots from the fibronectin stock solution, set aside for immediate use, and freeze remaining aliquots for future use.
Unwrap the outer covering of aluminum foil before placing the glass slide into a biosafety cabinet.
Place the glass slide into a sterile rectangular 4-well cell culture dish in the biosafety cabinet.
Dilute fibronectin stock solution 1:100 with distilled water in the biosafety cabinet.
Coat each slide with 1 mL of diluted fibronectin, drop by drop using a pipette, ensuring complete coverage.
Incubate the slides in a tissue culture incubator at 37 °C for 24 - 48 hours.
Aspirate fibronectin by tilting the 4-well cell culture dish.
Avoid touching the slide directly with the aspirator.
Count human endothelial cells and seed approximately 1.0 x 10^6 cells onto each fibronectin-coated glass slide with 1 mL of media (1.0 x 10^6 cells/mL media).
Seed cells 24 h prior to the anticipated application of laminar flow.
Let cells adhere to the slide for 15 min at 37°C.
Add 3 mL of media in each well of the cell culture dish to cover the slide.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 24 h with 5% CO2.
Seed human endothelial cells in antibiotic-free media at 750,000 to 1 x 10^6 cells per slide to achieve 85% - 95% confluence the next day.
Design custom siRNAs or order premade siRNAs for the gene of interest.
Add 6 μL of siRNA (20 µM stock) in 414 μL of reduced serum medium and mix gently by pipetting.
Dilute 49.5 µL of lipid-based transfection reagent in 130.5 µL of reduced serum medium and mix gently.
Incubate the diluted siRNA-lipid mixture for 5 min at room temperature.
Combine diluted siRNAs and lipid-based transfection reagent, mix gently, and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Remove growth medium and wash cells once with reduced serum medium.
Add 2.4 mL of reduced serum medium to each slide.
Add 600 μL of siRNA-lipid complex mixture to each plate and rock the plate back and forth to mix.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C for 4 h.
Add 1 mL of antibiotics-free endothelial cell growth media with 3x normal concentration of FBS without removing transfection mixture.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C until ready to use.
Set up a dedicated environment for monitoring system and multiple parallel-plate flow chambers.

Use a large heated unit/incubator with multiple shelves, internal electricity access, and glass doors to house multiple flow chambers simultaneously for experiments requiring both shear stress and direct comparison between treatments or outputs.
Ensure adequate CO2 is available for the experiment.
Ensure the water tray is appropriately filled for humidified air.
Autoclave the flow chamber plates.
Autoclave the reservoir.
Autoclave the dampener.
Autoclave the tubing.
Autoclave the Luers for each parallel-plate flow chamber set-up.
Place sterile towels into the biological safety cabinet.
Assemble the flow loop system without the parallel-plate flow chamber in the biological safety cabinet.
Insert a #14 hard tube into one hole of the cap of the flow reservoir.
Insert two #14 soft tubes into the other two holes in the cap of the flow reservoir.
Ensure that one of the soft tubes touches the bottom of the reservoir as outflow tubing.
Place a 1/16” male Luer at the end of the #14 hard tube and attach a sterile filter as an air vent.
Place a 1/16” female Luer at the end of the #14 soft inflow tube and attach a 4-way stopcock.
Place a 1/16” male Luer at the end of the #14 soft outflow tube.
Connect the reservoir outflow tubing to pump tubing using 1/16” female Luers at each end of a #13 hard tube and connecting it with the #14 soft outflow tube from the reservoir.
Attach the pump tubing with ‘dampener bridge’ tubing by placing 1/8” male and female Luers at each end of a #16 soft tube and connecting them to the ends of the pump tubing.
Assemble tubing for the flow dampener using a 3/16” male Luer at one end of the #25 soft tubing, repeating this for both sides of the flow dampener.
Attach the free ends of the #25 soft tubes to each side of the flow dampener.
Connect the ‘dampener bridge’ tubing with tubing for the flow dampener using a 1/8” female Luer from the #16 ‘dampener bridge’ side and a 3/16” male Luer from the #25 soft dampener tube side.
Assemble ‘chamber bridge’ tubing by placing a 1/8” female and male Luer at each end of a #16 soft tube.
Connect the 1/8” female Luer of the ‘chamber bridge’ with the 3/16” male Luer from the free end of the flow dampener.
At the 1/8” male Luer (free end) of the ‘chamber bridge’ tubing, place a 4-way stopcock.
Connect the 4-way stopcock from the ‘chamber bridge’ free end to the 4-way stopcock from the reservoir inflow soft tubing.
Close the stopcocks.
Add media to the reservoir and dampener.
For a 48-h exposure to shear stress, add 35 mL of media to the reservoir and 25 mL to the dampener.
Adjust the volume of the media based on the duration of the flow experiment and the number of cells seeded.
Place the #13 hard tube (pump tubing) into the pump head and secure it.
Open the stopcocks.
Turn on the pump and slowly increase the pump speed.
Let the media circulate through the loop system.
Check for any leakage or blockage, such as pressure build-up.
Ensure that the media is flowing back to the reservoir.
Place a 1/8” female Luer at one end of a #16 soft tube and attach a 4-way stopcock.
Attach the free end of the tube to the right side of the top plate (inflow side).
Place a 1/8” male Luer at one end of a #16 soft tube and attach a 4-way stopcock.
Attach the free end of the tube to the left side of the top plate (outflow side).
Place a 1/8” male Luer and a 1/8” female Luer at each end of a #16 soft tube (bubble trap tubing).
Attach the tubing to bubble trap via the 1/8” male Luer.
Attach a 4-way stopcock to the other end of the tubing via the 1/8” female Luer.
Using sterile tweezers, transfer the cell-seeded glass slide from the 4-well cell culture dish to the recess on the bottom plate.
Ensure the cell-seeded side of the glass slide is facing up.
Add 10 mL of warm media to the bottom plate within the red gasket line around the plate.
Allow the media to flow through the slide and cover the cells.
Avoid adding media directly onto the slide.
Gently place the top plate onto the bottom plate, aligning from one side to the other.
Avoid the introduction of air bubbles.
Screw the plates together tightly.
Remove air bubbles from the bubble trap by opening the stopcock on the right side (inflow) of the plate and gently flushing 20 mL of warm media using a 30-mL syringe.
Make sure the stopcock on the left side (outflow) of the plate is closed and that the media is flowing through the bubble trap stopcock (open).
Discard the flushed media.
Close the stopcock on the bubble trap and open the stopcock on the left side (outflow) of the chamber.

Elevate the left side (outflow) of the chamber to a 45° angle and gently flush 20 mL of warm media using a 30-mL syringe from the right side (inflow) of the chamber to remove air bubbles from the chamber.
Bubbles can be visualized through the window.
Discard the flushed media.
Close the stopcocks on both sides of the chamber and cap.
Inspect the cells by microscopy.
Transport the chamber to the BEACH with the previously assembled loop system.
Decrease the pump speed and pause the pump.
Close the stopcocks on the flow loop system to prevent leakage.
Connect the chamber and loop system together via stopcocks.
Open all the stopcocks.
Increase the pump speed slowly and examine for leakage or blockage.
Ensure media circulates in one direction and returns to the reservoir.
Place the flow sensor on the 'chamber bridge' tubing located on the inflow side of the chamber.
Orient the sensor properly in the direction of flow.
Adjust the pump speed to obtain the calculated flow rate based on desired shear stress.
Turn on the CO2 tank to achieve 5% CO2 and place a water tray inside the BEACH.
Harvest cells from the flow chamber once the desired time period is complete.
Decrease peristaltic pump speed to zero and turn off the power.
Close all open stopcocks quickly.
Remove the chamber and attached tubing with a stopcock on each end.
Take the chamber to a clean benchtop.
Unscrew all screws to remove the top plate from the bottom plate.
Using needle-nose tweezers, remove the glass slide from the bottom plate.
Place the glass slide into a 100 mm diameter tissue culture dish.
Wash the slide with 10 mL of cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Check the cells under a microscope to confirm cell adherence and alignment in the direction of flow.
Aspirate the PBS from the plate.
Transfer the slide to a clean 100 mm diameter dish.
Add 350 µL of lysis buffer containing 1/100 beta-mercaptoethanol to the slide.
Scrape the cells off the slide using a polyethylene-bladed cell scraper.
Pipette the cell lysate into a 1.5-mL tube and keep it on ice.
Dilute stock exogenous reference RNA (luciferase RNA) to 0.0025 ng/µL through serial dilution.
Add 10 µL of diluted luciferase RNA to each sample of cell lysate.
Proceed with the RNA extraction protocol as per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Freeze the lysate at -80 °C until able to proceed with the extraction.
Determine the total amount of luciferase copies added per sample.

Calculate the molecular mass of the luciferase RNA using an average molecular mass per nucleotide of 330 g/mol and multiplying it by the length of the firefly luciferase RNA, which is 1652 nucleotides.
Divide the amount of luciferase RNA added (0.025 ng) for each sample prior to RNA extraction by the molecular mass to yield the molar quantity.
Multiply the molar quantity by Avogadro’s number to yield the copies added per sample.
Calculate the theoretical yield for the luciferase copies for each RT-qPCR reaction using a specific equation.
Generate a standard curve for RT-qPCR using the luciferase plasmid to calculate the experimental yield for the luciferase copies for each RT-qPCR reaction.
Calculate the luciferase efficiency (%) using an appropriate equation.
